extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering containing 12,247 multiple-choice questions generated from ConceptNet to test commonsense knowledge.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crowd-workers author multiple-choice questions based on subgraphs extracted from ConceptNet. Each question set includes a source concept and three target concepts with the same semantic relation. Workers formulate three questions (one per target concept) and add two distractors per question (one from ConceptNet, one manually authored). Questions are verified by another group of workers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data is collected from ConceptNet, a graph knowledge-base with 32 million triplets representing commonsense relations between concepts. Subgraphs are extracted with one source concept and three target concepts sharing the same relation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Triplets from ConceptNet are filtered to remove general relations (e.g., RelatedTo), relations well-explored in NLP (e.g., IsA), concepts longer than four words or not in English, and triplets with low edit distance between concepts. This results in 236,208 triplets used for question generation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions are verified by workers; each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker who answered correctly are used (filtering out 15% of questions). Textual context is added by querying Google search for each question and candidate answer, retrieving the first 100 result snippets per answer candidate (500 snippets total per question).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers author questions and annotations (correct answers and distractors). Workers are instructed to avoid surface clues and create questions requiring commonsense knowledge. Questions are verified by another group of workers who annotate questions as unanswerable or choose the right answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used. This process filters out 15% of questions. Human accuracy on a sample of 100 questions is 88.9% based on majority vote from five workers not involved in generation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question has one correct answer and four distractors (two from the original target concepts, one additional from ConceptNet, one manually authored). Verification involves 2 annotators per question.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance natural language understanding by testing commonsense knowledge, which is critical for AI systems to interact more naturally with humans. It highlights gaps in current models' ability to handle commonsense reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases from ConceptNet and crowd-worker generation, but specific biases are not discussed. The paper notes that workers were instructed to avoid surface clues to reduce simple associative biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are generated from ConceptNet, which may limit coverage of commonsense phenomena. The dataset focuses on multiple-choice format with five answers per question. Performance of models is substantially below human accuracy (55.9% vs. 88.9%), indicating generalization limits. Non-recommended uses are not specified.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for commonsense question answering models. The dataset is used to evaluate state-of-the-art NLU models like BERT, GPT, and others. Usage guidelines include splits for random and question concept disjoint evaluation.
